title: {{NAME}} and the Kingdom's Three Powers
moral: The realm is safest when its protectors trust each other completely.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a deep royal burgundy hero coat with silver emblem, armoured dark trousers, and burgundy-silver boots — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The kingdom of Ironhaven had three protective forces.

The Royal Guard (Princess Tamsin's authority). The Hero Corps (the professional hero organisation). And the unicorn Meridian (who worked independently but cooperated with both).

For three years, they had operated separately, aware of each other, never formally coordinating.

Until the storm.

A catastrophic weather event hit the southern coast: flooding, evacuations needed, three different crises happening simultaneously.

{{NAME}}, who worked as a communications specialist for all three, sent one message to all three at the same time:

You need each other right now.

pages.content:
The coordination happened faster than he'd expected.

Princess Tamsin directed the Royal Guard to the inland flooding, where organisation and resources were the primary need.

The Hero Corps handled the coastal rescue, where physical capability and fast action were required.

Meridian moved between both zones: her horn's healing properties treating injuries, her presence calming panicked animals and sometimes people.

{{NAME}} managed the communication between all three, relaying information across the three coordination systems simultaneously.

He hadn't slept in twenty-four hours. He didn't notice.

pages.content:
At hour eighteen, the three forces met physically for the first time: a crossover point where the inland flooding met the coastal rescue zone.

Princess Tamsin, the Hero Corps commander, and Meridian stood in the same location, all looking at the same problem: a collapsed bridge blocking both zones' evacuation routes.

{{NAME}} had sent them all to the same coordinates at the same time. On purpose.

"Was this planned?" asked the Hero commander.

"I knew you'd all need to solve this one together," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The bridge took forty minutes.

Three-way coordination: the Royal Guard stabilised the structure, the heroes moved it, Meridian's energy helped with the final lift.

None of them could have done it alone.

All of them knew it.

Princess Tamsin looked at the Hero commander afterward.

"We should have done this years ago."

"We weren't ready," he said.

"What changed?"

Both of them looked at {{NAME}}.

"He made us ready," said Tamsin. "By making sure we were in the right place at the right time."

pages.content:
He slept for twelve hours straight when it was over.

Before falling asleep, he had written one note: formal coordination protocol meeting, two weeks.

Because the storm had shown it was possible. And possible things needed to be made permanent.

In his sleep, he heard the radio chatter of three forces talking to each other, not through him, directly, the way it should have always been.

He slept through all of it and woke up satisfied.
